correctness.rationale: Exact Farey denominator bijection yields the coprime lattice region. The Mobius cell-count argument has a rectifiable piecewise-monotone boundary and an error \(O(N^{1/\min(r,s)}\log(2N))\); the beta identity is exact. Fixed-threshold counts prove the limiting measure. Two separated cusp expansions with positive constants prove tail asymptotics and moment threshold. Reconstructed quantifiers: all fixed integers \(r,s\ge2\) and \(N\to\infty\); \(t\to\infty\) only after the probability limit. Independent finite enumeration checks 45 cases and a large-N regression; no numerical extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: Actual searches located the classical ordered Farey-neighbor criterion, unrestricted and parity-restricted gap laws, and unrestricted Farey denominator tables but no previously stated thin power-conditioned count plus universal cusp tail/moment threshold. Unlike a positive-density or unrestricted spacing law, the power-pair set has vanishing relative frequency, so restriction of that limiting measure is not valid. The explicit power-cusp asymptotics have been derived afresh. Residual unindexed-source risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Sparse two-sided power restrictions change the size scale of Farey neighbors to \(N^{1/r+1/s}\), and they cause an explicit family of heavy-tail exponents for normalized gaps; the associated sharp limiting-moment threshold is a natural structural invariant. This is not merely another unrestricted Farey denominator table or a routine constant recalculation: the cusp geometry explains the transition and supports future study of moments and extreme gaps in arithmetically thin Farey families. The proof is self-contained modulo the elementary Farey criterion and standard lattice method.
